requirements.evidence: Executable layout and compiler-interface audits enforce `http -> http3 -> quic_core` and reject the former package path.

Bounded body and common error tests now include supervised cleanup, exact concurrent cleanup outcomes, and separate source EOF, final wire result, and resource-release observations. Current-source full qualification and cross-protocol negative-case coverage remain required.

Source discovery finds {{http}} root, {{http3}} HTTP/3, and {{quic_core}} QUIC core tests. Native Windows reproduced the original 14 failures before fixes. The updated source must complete the independent three-package OS/OTP matrix and canonical-source verification before this baseline is Ready.
The private import allowlist contains {{boundary}} entries; source scan, compiler-interface audit, and compiled xref all reject any HTTP/3 dependency on `quic_core/internal/**`.

Grant-before-growth memory and connection admission now preserve typed memory refusal causes through retry/expiry races. New tests cover candidate socket cleanup, reciprocal connection-ID migration and retirement, pre-dial TCP admission, and shared HTTP/3 stream supervision. Full stability, hostile-peer, coverage, and platform qualification must be regenerated for the final source.

The unified HTTP/3 adapter now uses public streaming APIs with concurrent supervised upload and response reception. Authenticated connection selection, non-replayable uploads, origin/endpoint separation, shared admission, and reusable connections have focused regressions. Server reservations extend through response disposal and worker termination, with separate transfer and cleanup results. Client tracing, all lifetime races, platform evidence, and final API snapshots remain under qualification.

Strict heads/framing, verified active-once TCP/TLS paths, ordered finite pipelining, deferred Expect, half-close, pooling, and CONNECT/Upgrade streams have public tests. H1 responses now share the supervised source lifetime used for client uploads: peer TLS closure, listener stop, callback failure and deadlines cancel and join the producer. Input arriving during a pull remains bounded and preserves pipelining. Sixty-five scoped H1/TCP/TLS cases and old-server mutation controls validate the change; actual Chrome cancellation confirms source cleanup and worker exit. Listener handoff and finite phase counters remain observable. Current-source standards mapping, hostile matrices, independent-peer evidence, performance and platform qualification remain incomplete.

The active-once TLS client/server runtime, explicit cleartext prior knowledge, bounded frame/HPACK/SETTINGS/flow-control/stream queues, per-stream worker isolation and deadlines, fair response scheduling, RST/GOAWAY/PING/ORIGIN/priority behavior, Extended CONNECT opt-in, graceful drain, and sequential common-pool reuse are directly tested. ORIGIN advertisements are structurally bounded, server writes are fixed to stream zero, pool authority defaults to an exact authenticated origin key, and a 421 response evicts the connection. RFC 8336 records three explicit advisory deviations because peer advertisements do not yet enable cross-origin coalescing. The hostile-peer gate passes; remaining standards mapping, interoperability, performance, and platform qualification remain open.

The http3 package uses public quic_core streams, with supervised streaming upload, early responses, trailers, reuse, GOAWAY and listener lifetime tests. Native connection-ID issuance, routing, retirement and migration have live regressions. QUIC admission and send backpressure retain typed memory refusal and finite diagnostic chains. Cross-group and cookie-only HelloRetryRequest, retry PSK binders and ticket age, and post-retry early-data rejection have ordinary regressions and independent mutation checks. Chrome exposed and verified fixes for asymmetric Datagram SETTINGS and response cancellation after request FIN; bounded public send-completion observation connects the three API layers. Connection admission now prepays terminal history within a 64 KiB minimum grant, and active completion waiters reserve 8 KiB before their monitors exist. Public 65535/65536-byte boundaries, caller death, actual bounded storage and terminal-error classification have ordinary and mutation controls. Final current-source suites, coverage, rejection/release matrices and QPACK/RFC evidence still require qualification. The inventory maps {{mapped_standards}} RFCs and {{mapped_pinned_specifications}} pinned specifications; incomplete inventories are {{incomplete_standards}} RFCs and {{incomplete_pinned_specifications}} pinned specifications.

Structured Fields, digest/signature, Binary HTTP, OHTTP, compression, WebSocket and MASQUE have bounded codecs and public behavior tests. General Brotli compressed blocks have independent synthetic-corpus comparisons. Go and TypeScript OHTTP exercise three roles, two AEADs, bodies, trailers, tampering and verified outer TLS. Independent masque-go exercises concurrent CONNECT-UDP flows, datagram association, policy rejection and joined cleanup in both roles. MASQUE has 97 scoped live and native controls, including clock overflow, owner death, reordered activity, finite contention, one-shot stop notification, confirmed idle-owner exit and typed join timeout. Four isolated mutants prove the new lifetime controls detect their target faults. Cross-platform ECN wire observations, privileged ICMP delivery, independent CONNECT-IP, final-source extension coverage and complete extension RFC maps remain incomplete. RateLimit targets the pinned draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11.

The schema-4 inventory pins {{standards}} RFC rows and {{pinned_specifications}} immutable non-RFC specification revision(s), one IANA registry, qlog schema hashes, an official RFC catalog digest ({{rfc_catalog_sha256}}), official-source digests, role-specific BCP 14 dispositions (including REQUIRED/SHALL/RECOMMENDED aliases), per-document normative totals and level counts, evidence symbols, and reviewed errata counts. Twelve adversarial auditor cases reject false RFC identities, mutable draft names, undeclared empty maps, unknown roles, mandatory deviations, weak N/A rationales, normative count/level drift, errata-count drift, and missing symbols; two positive alias cases and an explicitly inventoried zero-clause RFC are also accepted. The inventory currently enumerates {{requirements}} atomic requirements and {{errata_reviewed}} reviewed errata across {{mapped_standards}} completed RFC maps and {{mapped_pinned_specifications}} completed pinned maps. {{requirement_breakdown}} `inventory_complete` is {{inventory_complete}}; {{incomplete_standards}} RFC maps and {{incomplete_pinned_specifications}} pinned maps remain incomplete.

{{coverage_summary}} Source discovery currently defines {{hostile_tests}} hostile tests in {{hostile_families}} families, and {{stability_targets}} stability targets requiring {{stability_executions}} isolated executions. PR property/fuzz campaigns configure 10,000 cases for each HTTP/3, QUIC and unified-HTTP family; full million-case shard evidence remains required. Common test runners retain bounded, redacted failure categories, exact generator leaf counts, actual VM exit and current-source bindings. Duplicate JSON keys, escaped duplicates, stale nonce, missing work, private fields and forged failure stacks have adversarial controls. Bootstrap synchronization separates trust-store preparation from public-connect ownership barriers; unchanged deadlines pass eight cold VMs on both Windows and Linux and reject missing-join mutants. Exploratory coverage and convergence captures are source-scoped; the 60-second instrumented settle budget, full 95%/90% and changed 100%/100% requirements remain unchanged. Complete final-source coverage, stability and hostile campaign reports are not yet available.

Pinned runners and source-scoped execution evidence exist for curl, nghttp2, aioquic, quic-go, quiche, ngtcp2/nghttp3, Go/TypeScript OHTTP and independent MASQUE. Go receipts bind source inventories, recipes, locks, actual compilation and executable bytes; the reader independently checks retained ELF build information. Frozen a15 retains two independent MASQUE roles and six scenarios each for Go and TypeScript OHTTP, while retaining its original core-suite failure. Source-tree bytecode generation is reproduced and prevented at tool entrypoints rather than hidden from source identity. Native MASQUE sidecars match embedded invocations and account for joined workers. Actual Chrome H1/H2/H3 transfer and cancellation diagnostics pass, including certificate-rejection controls; formal browser receipts, Firefox and the complete current-source peer matrix remain unfinished. Prior local credential and suite results do not replace the required six OS/OTP credential attestations or eighteen current-source package reports.

Bounded public H1/H2/H3 workloads have scoped frozen-source throughput, latency, sampled memory and convergence evidence. Fixed HTTP/3 workloads, idle wakeups and hot-path counters have retained execution verifiers. Matched independent-reference/baseline comparisons and all final-source performance thresholds remain unqualified. Prior reproducible archive and OTP consumer runs must be regenerated from the final canonical source with SBOM, provenance and the complete audit bundle.
Independent cryptographic, protocol, parsing, and resource-exhaustion attestations are external conditions and have not been supplied.

findings.evidence: The public core is limited to the audited quic_core, client, server, config, diagnostics, and failure modules with opaque connections and streams; API snapshots and public loopback tests cover the supported transport lifecycle.
findings.closure: Closed by the compiler-derived API audit, archive audit, and public-core behavior suites.

findings.evidence: HTTP/3 sessions, QPACK, Capsules, and workers are owned by the http3 package while QUIC packet, TLS, UDP, Retry, token, and connection state remain core-owned.
findings.closure: Closed by independent package builds, source/API boundary scans, compiled xref, and archive-content checks.

findings.evidence: Supervised connection actors, candidate admission, cancellation and cleanup have live regressions. New body-lifetime and idle-control findings show why prior closure cannot qualify changed source.
findings.closure: Close only after current-source hostile-peer isolation, owner-death, cleanup and finite-resource evidence passes; complete platform and coverage matrices remain separately required.

findings.evidence: Admission and later receive/send/mailbox growth reserve memory before allocation. Typed pressure causes and bounded retry/release have new regressions; final-source aggregate-pressure evidence is pending.
findings.closure: Regenerate current-source hostile-peer aggregate-memory, backpressure, parallel-progress, crash-release and client-refusal evidence before closing this finding.

findings.evidence: Scoped local credential suites cover certificate algorithms, mTLS, rotation, resumption and rejection. Cross-group and cookie-only HelloRetryRequest, ticket-age update and rollback, retry PSK binding and early-data rejection now have 104 scoped regressions and mutation checks; prior successes do not establish the complete current-source six-platform credential matrix.
findings.closure: Collect current-source Ubuntu 24.04, macOS 15, and Windows 2025 attestations on OTP 28 and 29 and pass credential-matrix aggregate verification.

findings.evidence: The finite monitored adapter receives only a domain-separated fingerprint and retention interval; rejection, error, exit, and timeout fail closed to authenticated 1-RTT fallback without losing PSK resumption.
findings.closure: Closed by direct adapter outcomes and public live accepted/rejected 0-RTT regressions.

findings.area: qlog schema, breadth, and qvis compatibility
findings.evidence: Prior qlog execution predates the current source. The validator now binds capture start/end and trace digests to the complete source identity; the live current-source capture and qualification report must be regenerated.
findings.closure: Regenerate a current-source Ready qlog-validate report with capture identity and retain writer failure/teardown evidence.

findings.evidence: The deterministic oracle remains implemented. Current-source execution, all eight million-transition shards, and the independently validated aggregate are required before closing this finding.
findings.closure: Run every declared current-source model shard and verify the complete million-transition aggregate.

findings.evidence: Static security, API/boundary, reproducible package, campaign, hostile/stability, qlog, model, examples, and OTP 29 release-simulation gates exist; coverage thresholds, complete RFC maps, expanded peers, cross-protocol performance, OTP 28, and canonical-archive qualification remain incomplete.
findings.closure: Make every non-external source-candidate gate Ready and retain reproducible current-source evidence, including the adaptive coverage and raw capture artifacts.

findings.evidence: Historical fixed-workload successes and newer frozen diagnostic measurements have different source and host conditions. Public protocol workloads, hot-path priming and idle-wakeup controls have scoped proofs, but all final-source fixed thresholds and matched comparisons have not passed.
findings.closure: Close only after the current-source performance audit verifies actual completed workloads, convergence and the required thresholds and comparisons, without reusing historical success as current proof.

findings.evidence: The local OTP 29 release simulation is reproducible, but no passing canonical-source candidate, OTP 28 rerun, third-party audit attestation, signed local commit, or clean-worktree proof exists.
findings.closure: Pass every automated gate from the canonical source archive, then obtain the external attestation and signed commit without tagging, publishing, uploading, or pushing.

findings.evidence: HTTP/3 consumes only the six public core modules and opaque connection/stream values; the allowlist contains comments only and source scan, package-interface audit, and compiled xref report zero private references.
findings.closure: Closed by the zero-entry three-layer boundary gate and public loopback coverage.
